mentions.name: Archme
mentions.description: Archme is a CLI tool that scans a codebase and generates permanent C4 and sequence diagrams, keeping them up to date on each commit. Code review then happens as small changes to diagrams instead of 10k-line pull requests. It runs on the user's own computer so code never leaves the machine.
mentions.problem: Code is no longer the right medium for understanding and collaboration in the era of AI and 10k-LOC pull requests.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I built a new abstraction layer for code (https:// www.archme.io), as I believe it's no longer the right medium for understanding and collaboration in the era of AI and 10k LOC PRs.

It scans your codebase, turns it into permanent c4 & sequence diagrams and keeps them up to date on each commit. Then, instead of reviewing a 10k line coding PR, you review a 30 line change to sequence and C4 diagrams.

npm i -g @archme/cli && archme init to run it on your own computer, code never leaves your machine.
